Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0057-erp-authorization-core-business-units-and-scope-depth.md, docs/adr/0147-membership-scoped-rls-lowers-to-an-engine-internal-org-member-semi-join-leaf.md, docs/adr/README.md + docs/adr/0139-engine-internal-semi-join-leaf-readable-parent-ids.md, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/formula/src/cel-to-filter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-rls-filter.ts, packages/spec/src/data/readable-ids.ts, packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-filter.ts, packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/odata-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/read-scope-sql.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/parent-record-read-gate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-run-as.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-member.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, scripts/adr-index.mjs

Inputs read: card #29360 (body, triage `6580364238`, claim `6581842163`, os-dev-report `6582668525`), PR #29501 (body, 3-file list, net diff against `main` at the merge-base `cafe8ee6`: +357 / -3), the check-runs on the head (every non-skipped run `success`: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Check Documentation Links, PR-body guards, Test Core, Type Check · workspace and the rest; none failed, none pending at the time of this record), the lane delta at `/mnt/project-files/spec-seat2/29360-delta.md`, and project memory `adr-amendment-note-recipe`. The live tree was read with `git show` at the head only.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set: no change.** The diff is `docs/adr/**` only (one new record, one appended blockquote, one regenerated index). No package, schema, test, gate or `scripts/adr-anchors/` entry changes. `pnpm check:adr-symbol-anchors`, `check:adr-index`, `check:adr-links` are the gates for these files and the head's check-runs are green. **Right.**
- **Public surface: nothing published.** `OrgMemberIds` and "the driver's compile declaration" are proposed names, not exports; `packages/spec` is untouched (no `OrgMemberIds` / `ActiveOrgMemberIds` exists in the tree). The PR's claim "No code, no schema, no test" matches the tree. **Right.**
- **ADR number 0147 is free** on `main` (highest is 0146) and the README gained exactly one row and the counts (147 → 148 records, Proposed 4 → 5). The row's title shows `currentuser.orguserids` because `scripts/adr-index.mjs` strips `_` (line 192) — the generator's behaviour, with precedent at ADR-0068's row (`currentuser`); not this PR's defect. **Right.**
- **The 0057 note landed in the right one of the two ADR-0057 records** (`-erp-authorization-core-…`, whose D3 bullet cites the cap). `f72bc9e5` is PR #29356's merge on `main`. **Right.**
- **Status is `Proposed`, the Status line of 0057 is untouched, no `Amended` keyword sits in the index window.** **Right.**
- **D-a/D-b/D-c read correctly off the live tree** (measured below in ④): `#resolveUserAuthzGrants` reads `sys_member { organization_id: tenantId }` through `#tryFind` with `{ isSystem: true }` and no `tenantId` (installation-wide, outside `applyTenantScope`), completes past 1,000 by keyset pages of `id`, keeps `user_id` values that are non-empty strings, adds the caller unconditionally, applies no validity / status / role filter to the organization's rows (ADR-0091 `isGrantActive` is applied only to the caller's own `sys_member` rows for `accessible_org_ids`); `#lowerMembership` emits `{ FIELD: { $in: value } }` and refuses a non-array; `#userContextOf` copies `org_user_ids` from the context; `resolveDelegatorContext` overwrites the delegator's list with the live principal's (`dctx.org_user_ids = context.org_user_ids`) under the delegator's `userId`. The ADR's reading of each is **right**.
- **D-e census corrections** verified by a tree-wide grep: `current-user-endpoints.ts` holds a comment only; `assemble-execution-context.ts` (L158 key list, L381 envelope), `service-automation/plugin.ts`, `run-resume.ts`, `runtime-identity.ts#runOrgUserIds` (answers `undefined` for a missing array), `share-link-service.ts`, `sharing-plugin.ts`, `runtime/src/domains/share-links.ts`, `mention-recipient-gate.ts`, `explain-engine.ts#buildContextForUser`, `objectql`'s `ScopedContext[SEED_USER_GRANTS]` (`needsPeers = !Array.isArray(ctx.org_user_ids)`, in `engine.ts`, keyed by the `hook-run-as.ts` symbol) are the readers and carriers. The one evaluator the census **misses** is named in ④ (must-fix 2). The write-verb question is closed by the tree: a predicate update/delete is narrowed by the read door's answer (`security-plugin.ts`, `id IN (the rows the read returned)`, cap `PREDICATE_WRITE_READABLE_ID_CAP`), never by the compiled RLS filter in the write's own `where`, so D-a's "legal only on `find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate`" loses nothing on `main`. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is correct: `docs/adr/**` publishes nothing, and the Check Changeset run on the head is `success`. `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and the claim matches: nothing is narrowed or widened in a published surface by this diff; the record itself says "Each execution card declares its own Clause-②", which is where the SQL-family card's past-ceiling 500 → answer belongs. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (no metadata-protocol surface touched). **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (os-dev-report `6582668525`):
1. `admin-set-user-manager.ts` comment left out, carried by V3 (O6) — **answered**: the delta allows exactly this ("If the comment edit in plugin-auth is outside the lane, list it in out_of_scope"); the quotation stays a quotation.
2. D-e corrected from the card — **answered, verified** (①).
3. Rules beyond the card ("an array wins over the anchor"; "the anchor's caller, never the compiling context's `userId`") — **answered, right**: both keep S byte-identical for every hand-built context and for the delegated explainer, whose `dctx` carries the live principal's list under the delegator's id (`explain-engine.ts` L897–898). A re-derived caller would swap the principal for the delegator in S.
4. MCP writes skipped; attribution and `Fixes #29360` on the body — process, no finding.
5. Second commit refines one D-d row — confirmed by `git log` (two commits over the merge-base).

Open questions (judged, not stood in for):
- **O1 — new public names (`OrgMemberIds` and the driver's compile declaration)**: a new export of `@objectstack/spec` beside `ReadableIds`, so a maintainer decision. Option **A** is the right shape (a branded value drivers recognise must be exported, as `ReadableIds` is; C would lock every third-party SQL driver onto the floor). The name is defensible; `ActiveOrgMemberIds` would say the binding, but S is "active org's members plus the caller" under either name, and the ADR says so. ⛔ **Escalate to the maintainer with the Tier H approval**: the record lands only under names the maintainer approves (the ADR says this itself, O1), and the declaration's name is deferred to S1, which is acceptable.
- **O2 — does D-d's departure from ADR-0139 D3 need a pointer on ADR-0139?** **Yes (B), and not only D3**: see must-fix 1. ADR-0139 D1 ends "⛔ No second leaf, no `EXISTS`, no correlated form." and D3 says "⛔ No `DriverCapabilities` bit returns … a bit the engine does not consult is inert". ADR-0147 adds a second leaf and a consulted driver declaration, states the D3 departure, never names the D1 one, and lands no pointer on ADR-0139. The repo's own precedent is ADR-0139 itself: it revisited ADR-0055 row (a) and ADR-0056's non-goal and made "one pointer each … landed with this record" part of its acceptance criteria. Prime Directive 13's letter is met by a new ADR; its last sentence ("A decision nobody can find is a decision that will be reversed") is not, while ADR-0139 D1 reads as absolute.
- **O3 (the ADR's O4) — freshness against the opt-in grants cache**: **A, not a set change.** `OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS` defaults to 0 (`resolve-user-grants-cache.ts`, Fork 4); with it on, the array may be as old as the entry (retired by any watched-object write on the same engine) and the leaf reads at statement time. S(org, caller) is the same function of the same inputs; only the inputs' age differs, and the staleness window is the cache's accepted contract. D-0's sentence ("the inputs' age, not the rule") is the right place and should stay. No separate escalation; the maintainer reads it in the record.

Security findings: withheld by the dev; none of my own beyond ④.

### ④ Design judgment

**The bar (triage `6580364238`): the record keeps EXACTLY the visible set #29281 holds.** I tried to break the same-set invariant against the live code at the head: the resolver (both legs, the completion read, the claim-drop re-resolution, the API-key refusal, the guest path), the lowering, the compiler's user context and polarity guard, group posture (`vetOrganizationClaim` in `single` admits the claim unvetted; in walled postures it drops to no active organization and S = `{caller}` — the anchor is captured after that re-resolution, so it agrees), NULL/blank `user_id` under `$not` (SQL `NOT IN` over a NULL-bearing subquery is UNKNOWN; the guard reproduces today's non-empty-string filter and keeps the negation total), the caller arm (today `ids.add(userId)` unconditionally; the leaf ORs `anchor.callerId`), the delegated explainer (above), the array-wins rule, the `isEmptyMembershipFilter` polarity guard (S is never empty on the leaf path, since it holds the caller; a context with no caller carries today's `[]` and takes the array path, so the guard keeps its answers), `sys_member`'s `(organization_id, user_id)` unique index (declared, `sys-member.object.ts` L414), soft-delete (none declared on `sys_member`, none applied by the engine), tenant wall (`readableIdsSubquery` applies `applyTenantScope` to its parent; D-b correctly forbids that here because the group-posture wall is `organization_id IN accessible_org_ids`), and the drivers (mongodb and odata refuse `ReadableIds` through `findMisplacedReadableIds`; memory evaluates in process; turso's remote transport compiles a resolved semi-join). **On the paths the record names, S is unchanged, both polarities, every posture.** D-0, D-a, D-b, D-c, D-f and D-g hold against the code they cite.

Two places the record's own invariant is falsified by the live tree, both repairable in the record:

**Must-fix 1 — ADR-0147 reverses ADR-0139 D1's "⛔ No second leaf" without saying so, and ADR-0139 carries no pointer.** `docs/adr/0139-…md` D1: "⛔ No second leaf, no `EXISTS`, no correlated form." D3: "⛔ No `DriverCapabilities` bit returns … a bit the engine does not consult is inert." ADR-0147 cites D1 for its brand device (L130) and for rejecting `EXISTS` (L301), states its D3 departure (D-d, "Builds on"), and never names D1's prohibition as revisited; its "Amends" header and Acceptance criteria list the ADR-0057-erp note only. On `main` after this PR, an Accepted record would read "no second leaf" with nothing pointing at the Proposed record that adds one. The repo's convention is the one ADR-0139 set when it revisited ADR-0055 (a) and ADR-0056: a dated one-line pointer on the older record, landed with the new one, named in the new record's "Amends" and Acceptance criteria. Fix: (a) ADR-0147 "Builds on"/"Amends" and D-a/D-d name ADR-0139 D1 ("no second leaf") and D3 ("no capability bit") as the two decisions this record revisits for this one leaf, with the reason (D1's reason — one meaning under one brand — is kept by giving the second meaning its own brand; D3's reason fails where a refusal is excluded); (b) append-only dated pointer notes under ADR-0139 D1's last paragraph and D3's capability-bit bullet, in the recipe's blockquoted `**Amendment note (2026-11-02, ADR-0147 — #29360).**` form, no Status-line edit; (c) Acceptance criteria name both pointers. (Answers O2 as B.)

**Must-fix 2 — D-d's evaluator census misses the analytics raw-SQL read-scope compiler, which today compiles the array and would refuse the leaf.** `packages/services/service-analytics/src/read-scope-sql.ts#compileScopedFilterToSql` compiles `security.getReadFilter(object, ctx)`'s answer to SQL for the native-SQL strategy; its `$in` arm binds one parameter per member (`val.map(vbind)`, L2193–2197 — the same ceiling the record retires on `driver-sql`), it throws `$in … needs an array (fail-closed)` for a non-array comparand, and it refuses a `ReadableIds` leaf at entry (L1059). It is neither a driver, nor a federated object, nor an in-process judge of `matchesFilterCondition`, so no row of the D-d table and no sentence of D-d reaches it. If V1 emits the leaf when the context carries the anchor, every analytics query that reads `sys_user` (or any object whose RLS names `org_user_ids`) is refused where today it answers — the exact "narrows S to an error" D-d forbids and D-0 ("every driver … every evaluator") promises against — and D-g pins none of it. Fix: a D-d row for the analytics read-scope compiler (compile the subquery in its own dialect, or the floor through the same substitution the engine seam makes, chosen up front), a D-g floor-parity pin on the native-SQL strategy, and the analytics lane added to Consumers and the execution plan (V2 or its own card). The record's second commit claims to name "every in-process judge of a compiled RLS predicate"; this compiler is the one evaluator of that predicate outside plugin-security and the drivers.

Should-fix (none changes S; each is a sentence or a row):
1. **The explain API's published `readFilter`.** `explain-engine.ts` L3141 publishes the composed predicate as `ExplainDecisionSchema.readFilter` (`z.unknown()`, "the machine artifact behind the prose"). Today that artifact carries the id array; a leaf there arrives at the wire unbranded as the anchor's shape. The record lists the explainer as a floor evaluator (judging records) but says nothing about what it publishes. State it: the explainer materialises and publishes the array (today's wire shape), or publishes the anchor and the V3 card declares the Clause-② for the `readFilter` consumer.
2. **Consequences over-claims the request path.** "The request path issues no membership read, on any request" and "A `sys_member` outage used to fail every request's resolution (503). Now it fails the reads that use the leaf … Fewer requests fail" are wrong against `#resolveUserAuthzGrants` Leg 1, which still reads `sys_member { user_id: userId }` on every request for `accessible_org_ids` and the roles. What goes is the organization-membership read; a `sys_member` outage still fails every request's resolution. Say "no organization-membership read" and drop the failure-surface claim or restate it.
3. **The nested case.** A `ReadableIds` leaf whose parent P is `sys_user` (or any object whose RLS names `org_user_ids`) carries this leaf inside its composed `scope` (ADR-0139 D2 step 3): `parent-record-read-gate.ts`, `attachment-access-hooks.ts` and `controlled_by_parent` compose from `getReadFilter(P)`. `driver-sql` compiles `leaf.scope` recursively (`readableIdsSubquery` → `applyFilters`), memory evaluates the scope in process, but the engine's floor substitution must descend into composed scopes and the D-g pins should include one nested fixture. Name it in D-d and D-g.
4. **The ADR-0057-erp amendment vs `adr-amendment-note-recipe`.** The note form, placement and `path#symbol` anchor are right; the file's own header convention for an amendment is the inline `**Amended** (date, ADR-NNNN …)` entry on the Status line (ADR-0131's sits there), and the record carries no header pointer to D3's note. The recipe says: when the acceptance says no other text changes, leave Status alone and put the Status-line question in `open_questions` — the dev did the first and not the second. Put the one-entry Status-line pointer to the seat/maintainer explicitly (appending after the ADR-0131 entry is safe for `scripts/adr-index.mjs`, which keys on the EARLIEST keyword, `Accepted`).
5. **Anchor precision in D-e.** The "needs peers" probe lives in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (`ScopedContext[SEED_USER_GRANTS]`), keyed by the `hook-run-as.ts` symbol the record cites; cite the implementation site too so the V3 card lands on it.

## 待裁：ADR-0147 的新公开名字与一处有意保留的不对称（#29360）

- 一句话问题：大组织里"能看见本组织成员"这条行级权限，现在要先把全体成员 id 读出来塞进查询，成员一多就慢，过了数据库参数上限就直接报错。ADR-0147 提议让 SQL 驱动改成子查询直接算，看见的人一个不多一个不少。落地要在 `@objectstack/spec` 新增公开名字，另有一处不对称需要您定。
- 背景：分诊 6580364238 定"可见集合必须与 #29281 现状完全一致"。席位契约复审（6583043471）确认可见集合不变；本轮判 FAIL 是因为两处清单遗漏，都在 ADR 文字里修，开发已在改。ADR 属治理路径，另需 GOVERNED_APPROVERS 批准。
- 问题一：新叶子的名字（暂名 `OrgMemberIds`，与已有的 `ReadableIds` 并列导出），以及驱动"能否编译它"的声明（名字留到 S1 卡再定）。
  - A 保留 `OrgMemberIds`：直说"组织成员 id"，与 `ReadableIds` 成对，零额外工作。
  - B 改名（例如 `ActiveOrgMemberIds`）：点明只算当前组织，更精确但更长；改名只动 ADR 文字，约十分钟。
- 问题二（ADR 的 O3）：`org_user_ids` 不读 ADR-0091 的有效期窗口，而 `accessible_org_ids` 会读。今天 `sys_member` 没有有效期字段，所以没有任何一行的结果不同。
  - A 保留不对称：可见集合今天完全不变，ADR 记录下来，等 `sys_member` 真的加了有效期再议。
  - B 现在就对齐：将来 `sys_member` 一加有效期，可见集合就会变，这属于权限边界的变化，需要单独立卡。
- 推荐：问题一选 A，问题二选 A。盲区：将来如果出现"跨组织成员"的叶子，`OrgMemberIds` 会显得含糊，那时再给新叶子起新名即可。
- 自检：只看①选 A；②③④ 是否翻转：否。
- 落地：此 PR 保持草稿，等标签取下且 GOVERNED_APPROVERS 批准。

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `723e27a6b8ab7580eeb451c4c7781e049044248e`
Local-runs: none
Delta on: the FAIL record [`6583043471`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/29501#issuecomment-6583043471) at `f3a117fbe05b586e75ca0cbfd578d6fc61e7c4ae`. The delta is two commits (`e0104338`, `723e27a6`), `docs/adr/**` only: `0147-…md` +68/−27, `0139-…md` +11/−0, `0057-erp-…md` 1 line (the Status line, appended). No package, schema, test, gate or `scripts/` change; `docs/adr/README.md` is unchanged in the delta (judged right below). The live tree was read with `git show` at the head only.
Inputs read: the FAIL record in full; `git diff f3a117fb..723e27a6`; the head's check-runs (44; every non-skipped run `success` at the time of this record — Test Core was `in_progress` on first read and `success` on re-read; Check Changeset `skipped` by its job-level `if: !contains(labels, 'skip-changeset')` in `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`, the label being on the PR — the opt-out working as designed, not a failure); the card thread after 16:30Z (os-dev-report `6582668525`, the decision request `6583078458` and its withdrawal `6583516156`, "prompted by the maintainer's question at 2026-11-02T17:03Z"); project memory `adr-amendment-note-recipe`; `scripts/adr-index.mjs` at the head.

### ① The two must-fixes — both closed

**Must-fix 1 (ADR-0139 D1/D3 revisited without saying so, no pointer) — closed.** ADR-0147's header now says it: "Builds on" names the two prohibitions it revisits for this one leaf, with anchors into D-a and D-d; "Amends" lists three places (ADR-0139 D1, ADR-0139 D3, ADR-0057-erp D3), "each by a dated, append-only pointer note and nothing else", and says which Status lines move (0057-erp: one inline entry) and which do not (0139). D-a gains the bullet "A second leaf, so ADR-0139 D1 is revisited for it", with D1's reason (one brand, one meaning) and why it is kept (the second meaning gets its own brand, never a mode of `ReadableIds`); D-d's "Chosen up front" bullet now states the D3 revisit with D3's reason (an unconsulted bit is inert) and why it fails here (a refusal is excluded, so the engine must know before the call). Acceptance criteria name the three notes. On ADR-0139 the two notes sit where the FAIL record asked: directly under D1's last paragraph (the one ending "⛔ No second leaf, no `EXISTS`, no correlated form.") and under D3's capability-bit bullet, as a 2-space-indented blockquote inside that bullet (so it renders inside the list item). Both are dated `2026-11-02`, name ADR-0147 and #29360, and say exactly what is revisited and what stands. The 0139 edit is +11/−0: no Accepted sentence is rewritten, the Status line (L3–L10) is untouched, and the README's 0139 row is unchanged. **Closed, and O2 is answered as B.**

**Must-fix 2 (the analytics raw-SQL read-scope compiler missing from D-d) — closed.** D-d's table gains the row for `packages/services/service-analytics/src/read-scope-sql.ts#compileScopedFilterToSql`: floor, chosen up front, with the reason (handed the leaf it would refuse every analytics read of `sys_user` that answers today) and the later-card note (O7). Its three code claims hold at the head: the `$in` arm throws `needs an array (fail-closed)` on a non-array comparand (L2194) and binds one parameter per member (`val.map(vbind)`, L2197); the entry refuses a `ReadableIds` leaf by name (`findReadableIdsLeaf`, L843–851). The lane is added where the FAIL record asked: Consumers (`@objectstack/service-analytics` (its native-SQL read-scope compiler)), V1's "What lands" (`domain:services`, `service-analytics`) and its pins (`analytics`), D-g (the "Analytics" pin: a native-SQL query over `sys_user` answers the same rows as a direct `find` and is never refused), Consequences ("the analytics read-scope compiler takes the floor … four lanes"), and O7. **Closed.**

### ② The five should-fixes — all closed

- **(a) `readFilter`** — closed. D-d gains "What the explainer publishes": as a floor evaluator it materialises the array and **publishes the array**, today's wire shape; ⛔ never the leaf; no Clause-② is owed for a `readFilter` consumer. The anchor is right: `packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts#ExplainDecisionSchema` carries `readFilter: z.unknown().optional()` (L398), published by `explain-engine.ts` L3141. D-g gains the "Explain" pin (byte-identical `readFilter` for the same fixture); V1 says "the explainer publishes it".
- **(b) Consequences** — closed. "Positive" now says the request path issues no read of the **organization's** membership, and names Leg 1 of `#resolveUserAuthzGrants` as still reading the caller's own `sys_member` rows on every request; "Failure surface" is now "Unchanged in kind: a `sys_member` outage still fails every request's resolution (503) through Leg 1's own read", and a subquery failure fails that read with the driver's envelope, "never a shorter list".
